requiredMethods.expectation: null, true, false, zero, signed safe-integer extrema and NFC strings return the explicit corresponding built-in values.
Empty/nested arrays and sorted-key objects return explicit independent values, not candidate-produced expected values.
Compact JSON plus one LF raises ConformanceError(PROXY_NONCANONICAL_BYTES, fixed proxy refused; no execution authority).
Spaces, CRLF, key-order changes, alternative escaping and trailing content retain NON_CANONICAL_JSON or INVALID_JSON as appropriate; classify each fixed raw input independently.
Nested/top-level duplicate key a raises DUPLICATE_JSON_MEMBER with message duplicate member 'a'.
Invalid UTF-8 raises INVALID_UTF8: document is not UTF-8, after the initial wire-size gate.
Truncated/invalid strict JSON raises INVALID_JSON: document is not valid strict JSON.
Decimal/exponent/nonfinite forms raise NON_CANONICAL_NUMBER: floating-point values are not permitted.
Bytes safe integer extrema accepted; +/-9007199254740992 raises INTEGER_OUT_OF_RANGE: integer exceeds the canonical safe range.
NFD strings/keys raise NON_NORMALIZED_STRING; escaped lone surrogates preserve UnicodeEncodeError rather than being relabeled.
Empty/over-limit bytes and nonpositive exact-int maximum raise PROXY_DATA_SIZE before parsing; malformed oversized bytes therefore report size first.
16 nested arrays ending in null accepted with adequate budget;17/32 fail PROXY_DATA_TYPE;33 fails DOCUMENT_TOO_DEEP during initial canonical parsing.
4096 array entries accepted with adequate maximum;4097 fails COLLECTION_TOO_LARGE. Dict member-boundary rows use separately generated unique, sorted keys.
Object/list aggregate-budget and post-canonical encoded-size failures retain PROXY_DATA_SIZE and their original order; add combined-fault cases.
Bytes over canonical MAX_FILE_BYTES with larger declared maximum fail DOCUMENT_TOO_LARGE; do not confuse this with proxy maximum.
All fixed rejection vectors compare exception class, reason, message and first failing boundary; native UnicodeEncodeError/TypeError remain native exceptions.
bytes subclasses follow original fallback and fail PROXY_DATA_TYPE; never enter exact-bytes optimization.
bytearray and memoryview fail PROXY_DATA_TYPE through unchanged fallback.
dict/list/str/int subclasses retain PROXY_DATA_TYPE fallback behavior.
b'0', True succeeds as0; b'0',False fails PROXY_DATA_SIZE; bool is never exact-int fast path.
b'0',1.0 retains accepted fallback value0; unsuitable strings/None preserve TypeError.
An int subclass retains original fallback and any declared operator side effects.
A fixed maximum test double accepting one byte records ordered calls ge(1), sub(1), ge(1) on b'0'; failing first comparison stops before parsing.
For ordinary dict/list input retain the entire original function suffix and detached-copy semantics; do not optimize object input.
Changing caller-owned nested dict/list after return cannot change the returned graph.
Changing returned nested containers cannot change the caller input or a later result.
Repeated identical bytes produce equal values but distinct mutable graphs; there is no cross-call cache.
Subsequent changed/malformed byte inputs are revalidated; an earlier success never bypasses rejection.
Runtime prefix/suffix/imports/signature/defaults fixed; candidate function exact digest. Test/doc old prefixes immutable; appended IDs/definitions closed.
All135 paths and all132 non-owned files match exact mode,size,SHA256,Git blob; missing/extra/duplicate/symlink/hardlink/stale-current rows reject.
Independent assemblers mutate current source and update their claimed digests; unknown region, wrong before-image, copied proof, changed old test or source outside document still reject.
Existing three stage3 paths remain inside the original path graph; every old consumer/proof/fixture byte unchanged. Fresh current collection includes1277 old plus32 new methods.
